CVE-2026-117645.title: Phoenix.HTML vulnerable to attribute injection via unvalidated attribute names in attributes_escape/1
CVE-2026-117645.description:
Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix_html allows an attacker who controls attribute names to inject attributes and script into rendered HTML via Phoenix.HTML.attributes_escape/1.

attributes_escape/1 in lib/phoenix_html.ex escapes attribute values but not attribute names. key_escape/1 passes a binary key through html_escape, which neutralizes quotes and angle brackets but not whitespace, so a key such as x onmouseover ends the attribute and starts a new one. An atom key is only dasherized, so any character passes, including quotes and >. Nested data, aria and phx keys take the same paths. An application is affected when it builds attribute keys from untrusted input and renders them through HEEx <tag {@attrs}>, content_tag/3, or a direct call. Before 3.0.0 the same code lived in Phoenix.HTML.Tag.

This issue affects phoenix_html: from 1.0.0 before 3.3.5 and from 4.0.0 before 4.4.0.

CVE-2026-133755.title: Mailer Trusts Replies That a Man in the Middle Injects Right After STARTTLS
CVE-2026-133755.description:
Since Symfony 7.3, the require_tls option of EsmtpTransport refuses to send a message over a connection that isn't encrypted. It prevents a network attacker from stripping STARTTLS. But after the server's 220 reply to STARTTLS, the transport started the TLS handshake without checking whether more data had already arrived.

An attacker in the middle of the connection could add cleartext replies right after the 220. The transport then read them as if they came from the encrypted session. The attacker could make the transport skip AUTH, or report a message as sent while the server had rejected it.

Connections that use implicit TLS, with smtps:// or port 465, are not affected. Since Symfony 8.1, the Amazon SES SMTP transport enables require_tls by default on ports other than 465 and 2465. So ses+smtp:// DSNs are affected without setting the option.

The transport now refuses to start TLS when the server sends data right after its answer to STARTTLS, and throws a TransportException…

CVE-2026-63386.title: js-toml: Uncontrolled recursion in `load()` causes `RangeError` (stack exhaustion) on deeply nested input
CVE-2026-63386.description: js-toml is a TOML parser for JavaScript. Prior to 1.1.3, load() does not bound nesting or dotted-key depth in the recursive parser at src/load/parser.ts or the interpreter at src/load/interpreter.ts, so deeply nested arrays, deeply nested inline tables, or long dotted keys can exhaust the V8 call stack and throw a raw RangeError instead of the documented SyntaxParseError. Applications that parse attacker-controlled TOML and handle only SyntaxParseError can rethrow the unexpected exception, which can terminate a worker or process and cause denial of service. The exception is synchronous and catchable by consumers that handle all exceptions, and the issue does not affect confidentiality or integrity. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.3.

CVE-2026-64668.title: pam_usb: deny_remote bypassed by zone-indexed IPv6 addresses (fe80::1%eth0) in pusb_tmux_has_remote_clients
CVE-2026-64668.description: pam_usb provides hardware authentication for Linux using removable media. From version 0.8.0 to before version 0.9.3, the deny_remote feature in pam_usb uses /usr/bin/w -i to detect whether the authenticating user has an active remote tmux session. In pusb_tmux_has_remote_clients() (src/tmux.c), the IPv6 detection pattern matched the address group and then immediately expected whitespace. On Linux systems with multi-homed network interfaces, w -i appends a zone index (scope identifier) to link-local IPv6 addresses — e.g. fe80::1%eth0. The %eth0 suffix appeared between the address and the next whitespace field, causing the regex match to fail even for an otherwise-matching remote session. The function returned "no remote clients" and granted access. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.3.

CVE-2026-74760.description:
Google::Auth versions from 0.11 through 0.12 for Perl accept an authorization code from any local process because the gcloud-auth login callback does not check the OAuth state.

The gcloud-auth login and application-default login commands send a state parameter with the authorization request, then take the code from the first request to reach their loopback listener without comparing the returned state.

A local attacker can submit an authorization code for their own Google account. The CLI exchanges it and stores the refresh token as the user's credentials, so the user's tools then act as the attacker's account.

CVE-2026-99417.title: ovl: fix a torn path in ovl_get_redirect()
CVE-2026-99417.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: fix a torn path in ovl_get_redirect()

A hard link of a metacopy file that races with a rename of an ancestor
stores a redirect to the wrong lower file.

Each component of an absolute redirect must be the name that a dentry
has in the parent that the walk continues with. ovl_get_redirect()
copies the name under d_lock and calls dget_parent() after the unlock,
and the callers for a hard link hold no lock that stops a rename across
directories. A rename between the two steps combines the old name with
the new parent.

With delays in ovl_get_redirect(), an unprivileged user hard-linked a
metacopy file while renaming its ancestor to another directory, the
stored redirect named another lower path, and after a remount the file
showed the data of a root-only file.

Fix this by taking the parent first and checking it again under d_lock.

CVE-2026-99664.title: mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask()
CVE-2026-99664.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask()

follow_pud_mask() reads the PUD without a lock. If it is a leaf, it takes
the lock and calls follow_huge_pud(), which reads the entry again, but
only tests whether it is present.

A leaf can be zapped concurrently and a page fault can fill the empty
entry with a page table.

This currently only applies when device-dax makes use of PUD entries,
and the fault after e.g., MADV_DONTNEED would find THPs to be disabled.

That requires a sequence like

1) Fault in the PUD
2) Disable THP
3) Have GUP race against concurrent MADV_DONTNEED + refault

Which is rather unlikely to happen in practice, which is why we never
received a report about such a problem.

Before commit 1b1676180246 ("mm/gup: handle huge pud for
follow_pud_mask()"), we performed that check in follow_devmap_pud() by
testing for pud_devmap().

Let's fix it by just structuring follow_pud_mask() similar…
